acceptance: The edge worker is forked like the API worker and stays idle until the server is linked, entitled and remote access is enabled.

A wildcard certificate is issued through the cloud TXT record API with keys that never leave the host and renews with jitter; the HTTPS listener proxies to the API with forwarded headers and the via contract.

Disable or unlink removes the certificate and listener; shutdown closes sockets within five seconds; the public address is published through server config, the well-known document and the connections endpoint.

A custom public hostname on the owner's domain works through a CNAME to the relay name plus an _acme-challenge CNAME to the server's Frameleaf challenge name; a DNS check moves it from pending to verified and the server issues and renews its certificate.

acceptance: Setup claims an empty bucket with a root marker holding the instance id, refuses buckets claimed by another server or holding foreign objects, and probes customer-key encryption support.

A run writes the database dump, uploads only content hashes absent from the index as hash-named objects, then a manifest; a second unchanged run uploads nothing and identical files on the same server produce one object; runs survive restart and failures notify all administrators.
